rules:
OUTPUT SHAPE: exactly 5 lines, each terminated by a single LF (0x0A) INCLUDING the last one. Verified with `od -c`: N=1234/b=item output is `1234 items
 items
 3 items
 item
 1 item
` (34 bytes, 5 newlines). No CR, no BOM, nothing on stderr, exit status 0.

ITEM COUNT: count = (number of literal ',' bytes in the raw --a value) + 1. No stripping, no empty-item removal, no dedup. Observed: --a "" -> 1; --a "x" -> 1; --a " " -> 1; --a "," -> 2; --a "a," -> 2; --a ",a" -> 2; --a ",," -> 3; --a "a, b ,c" -> 3. Count 0 is therefore UNREACHABLE through this CLI (confirmed: --a "" prints `1 item` on line 1).
unit_len(seq, b) == str(len(seq)) + ' ' + cardinalize(b, len(seq)). The separator is EXACTLY ONE space (0x20) - confirmed by `cat -A` and `od -c` for 1-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 5- and 6-digit counts.

NUMBER RENDERING: plain base-10 `str(int)`. NO thousands separator, no grouping, no padding, no sign, no special-casing of any magnitude. Mechanically verified line-for-line for 238 distinct counts: every integer 1..200, 250..1000 step 50, 1023/1024/1025, 2000..10000 step 1000, 1234, 9999, 12345, 20000, 50000, 65535, 65536, 99999, 100000, 123456, 131071, 131072 -> 0 mismatches against the model `str(n)`. e.g. 1000 -> `1000 items`, 1234 -> `1234 items`, 9999 -> `9999 items`, 100000 -> `100000 items`, 131072 -> `131072 items`.
NUMBER RENDERING IS LOCALE-INDEPENDENT: with LC_ALL=C, LC_ALL=de_DE.UTF-8, LANG=en_US.UTF-8, PYTHONUTF8=1 the 1234-item run still prints `1234 items`.

SINGULAR/PLURAL SELECTION: cardinalize(word, count) returns `word` VERBATIM when count == 1, and pluralize(word) for every other observable count. Verified for count == 1 (singular), count == 2 (plural), and count == 131072 (plural), plus all 238 counts above. Counts 0 and negative are unreachable, so `count == 1` cannot be experimentally distinguished from `count <= 1`.

LINE-TO-COUNT MAP (full table for totals 1..6, b=item / b=mouse):  L1 count = total;  L3 count = min(total, 3);  L5 count = 1 always.  total=1: `1 item|item|1 item|item|1 item`; total=2: `2 items|items|2 items|item|1 item`; total=3: `3 items|items|3 items|item|1 item`; total=4: `4 items|items|3 items|item|1 item`; total=5: `5 items|items|3 items|item|1 item`; total=6: `6 items|items|3 items|item|1 item`. With b=mouse: total=1 -> `1 mouse|mouse|1 mouse|mouse|1 mouse`; total=2 -> `2 mice|mice|2 mice|mouse|1 mouse`; total=3 -> `3 mice|mice|3 mice|mouse|1 mouse`; total>=4 -> `N mice|mice|3 mice|mouse|1 mouse`.
LINE 3 uses the SINGULAR form only when the total is 1 (because len(items[:3]) == 1 then). LINE 5 always uses the singular form (len == 1 always).

LINE 4 (cardinalize(b,1)) IS ALWAYS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE RAW --b VALUE - no strip, no case change, no substitution. Verified exact bytes for: '  spaced  ' -> `  spaced  `; 'MiXeD' -> `MiXeD`; 'mice' -> `mice`; '' -> `` (empty line); ' ' -> ` `; '\ttab\t' -> `^Itab^I`; 'a b' -> `a b`; '%s{}%d' -> `%s{}%d`; 'a\\tb' -> `a\\tb`; embedded real newline 'a\nb' -> two physical lines. Same for LINE 5, which is `1 ` + raw --b (so --b '  spaced  ' yields `1   spaced  `).

TRAILING WHITESPACE only ever appears when --b itself contributes it via a verbatim path. --b '' with 4 items gives line 1 = `4 ` (digit, space, LF - od: `4  
  
 3  
  
 1  
`). --b '  MICE  ' gives `4   MICE  ` with two trailing spaces. Otherwise no line has trailing whitespace.

pluralize(word): let w = word.lower().strip(). (1) if w == '' -> return the ORIGINAL word verbatim (--b ' ' -> ` `, --b '   ' -> `   `, --b '' -> ``). (2) if w is a recognized PLURAL -> return the ORIGINAL word verbatim, un-stripped and un-recased ('  MICE  ' -> `  MICE  `, ' Mice ' -> ` Mice `, 'MicE' -> `MicE`). (3) otherwise build the plural from the STRIPPED, LOWERED w and then re-apply case ('  spaced  ' -> `spaceds`, '  CHILD  ' -> `CHILDREN`, '\ttab\t' -> `tabs`).

SUFFIX RULES on w (confirmed with synthetic nonsense stems zzz*/blorp*): ends with 'es' -> UNCHANGED (zzzes->zzzes, blorpes->blorpes, gles->gles, glaes->glaes, gloes->gloes); ends with consonant+'y' -> -y+'ies' (zzzy->zzzies, blorpy->blorpies) while vowel+'y' -> +'s' (zzzay->zzzays, zzzey->zzzeys, zzziy->zzziys, zzzoy->zzzoys, zzzuy->zzzuys); ends with 's'/'ch'/'sh' -> +'es' (zzzs->zzzses, zzzch->zzzches, zzzsh->zzzshes, gless->glesses); otherwise -> +'s'. NO -x and NO -z rule: zzzx->zzzxs, blorpx->blorpxs, zzzz->zzzzs, blorpz->blorpzs, box->boxs, kibbutz->kibbutzs.

CASE RE-APPLICATION, evaluated in THIS ORDER against the original --b string: if orig == orig.lower() -> result.lower(); elif orig == orig.upper() -> result.upper(); elif orig == orig.title() -> result.title(); else -> result unchanged (i.e. lowercase, since it was built from the lowered stem). Evidence: 'item'->`items`, 'ITEM'->`ITEMS`, 'Item'->`Items`, 'iTem'/'ITem'/'ITEm'/'chilD'/'ChilD'/'CHILd'->lowercase result, 'Item-A'->`Item-As`, 'O'Brien'->`O'Briens`, 'O'brien'->`o'briens`, 'Point-Of-Sale'->`Point-Of-Sales`, 'Abc1def'->`abc1defs`. Non-ASCII works: 'ÍTEM'->`ÍTEMS`, 'Ítem'->`Ítems`, 'CAFÉ'->`CAFÉS`.

The lower() branch is tested BEFORE upper(), so a caseless string takes the lower path: '123'->`123s`, '42'->`42s`, '0'->`0s`, '!!'->`!!s`, '-'->`-s`, '_x_'->`_x_s` (NOT uppercased). Only strings that are non-lower AND all-upper take the upper path: '3D'->`3DS`, 'X'->`XS`, 'ITEM-A'->`ITEM-AS`.

The irregular/plural lookup is on the WHOLE stripped+lowered --b string, never per-word: 'Big Child' -> `Big Childs` (not 'Big Children'), 'big child' -> `big childs`, 'BIG CHILD' -> `BIG CHILDS`, 'Field Mice' -> `Field Mices`, 'field mice' -> `field mices`, 'Data Point' -> `Data Points`, 'point-of-sale' -> `point-of-sales`.
DETERMINISTIC: 1545 probe rows contain 1425 distinct --b values with 120 repeats and ZERO conflicting outputs; repeated identical invocations always give identical bytes.

ARG ERRORS (not part of the 5-line output): missing --a/--b or an extra positional prints argparse usage + error to STDERR with exit code 2. `@file` response files are NOT supported (fromfile_prefix_chars is unset): `--a "@/tmp/f"` is treated as one literal item.
surprises: COUNT 1000001 IS UNREACHABLE through this CLI and I could not observe a 7-digit count. The Linux per-argument limit MAX_ARG_STRLEN = 131072 bytes caps --a: 131071 commas (131072 items) works, 131072 commas (131073 items) fails with `Argument list too long`. Max count actually observed = 131072, which still renders as plain `131072`. argparse has no fromfile_prefix_chars, so `@file` cannot be used to sidestep the limit. Conclusion on formatting is nevertheless safe: `str(n)` behaviour was confirmed across 1-6 digit magnitudes and is locale-invariant.

COUNT 0 IS UNREACHABLE: ''.split(',') == [''] so --a "" yields count 1 -> line 1 is `1 item` (SINGULAR). An implementation must not assume it can ever see 0 here; but if unit_len/cardinalize are exported, the count==1 vs count!=1 branch is all that is observable.

'Item1' -> 'Item1S' (capital S!). Because the case-matcher uses Python's str.title() on the lowercase result: 'item1s'.title() == 'Item1S' since title() capitalizes a letter following a digit. Likewise 'ITEM1' -> 'ITEM1S' but 'item1' -> 'item1s' and 'iTem1' -> 'item1s'.

The lower() test runs BEFORE the upper() test, so caseless strings are NOT uppercased: '123' -> '123s', '42' -> '42s', '0' -> '0s', '!!' -> '!!s', '-' -> '-s'. Getting this order backwards produces '123S'.

MIXED CASE IS DESTROYED, not preserved: 'MiXeD' -> 'mixeds', 'iTem' -> 'items', 'cHild' -> 'children', 'Item-a' -> 'item-as', 'O'brien' -> 'o'briens', 'Abc1def' -> 'abc1defs'. Only all-lower, all-upper and exact-title inputs keep their pattern.

ASYMMETRIC WHITESPACE HANDLING: the regular/irregular pluralization path STRIPS ('  spaced  ' -> 'spaceds', '  CHILD  ' -> 'CHILDREN'), but the already-plural path and the empty path return the ORIGINAL bytes verbatim ('  MICE  ' -> '  MICE  ', ' Mice ' -> ' Mice ', ' ' -> ' ', '' -> ''). So pluralize is NOT always strip-then-process.

--b '' makes line 1 end in a trailing space: the 4-item run is exactly `4 

3 

1 
`. Lines 2 and 4 are empty lines. An implementation that trims lines will diverge.
The irregular lookup key is the ENTIRE --b string, not the final word: 'Big Child' -> 'Big Childs' and 'Field Mice' -> 'Field Mices'. Do not tokenize.
'this' -> 'these' is in the table (a pronoun, not a noun) - easy to miss when generating candidate words.
-ae is a tiny closed set: alga/alumna/antenna/nebula/vertebra -> -ae, but formula -> 'formulas', larva -> 'larvas', persona -> 'personas', minutia -> 'minutias'.

Self-plural / plurale-tantum membership is arbitrary: 'means' -> 'means' and 'scissors' -> 'scissors' (both would be '...es' by rule), yet 'pants' -> 'pantses', 'news' -> 'newses', 'goods' -> 'goodses', 'jeans' -> 'jeanses', 'trousers' -> 'trouserses', 'thanks' -> 'thankses', 'darts' -> 'dartses', 'mumps' -> 'mumpses', 'billiards' -> 'billiardses', 'savings'/'earnings'/'belongings'/'surroundings'/'outskirts' -> '...es', and 'economics'/'physics'/'politics'/'ethics'/'statistics'/'mathematics'/'gymnastics' -> '...icses'.

Words ending 'es' pass through untouched even when clearly singular-ish or nonsense: 'series'->'series', 'species'->'species', 'shoes'->'shoes', 'clothes'->'clothes', 'riches'->'riches', 'premises'->'premises', 'glasses'->'glasses', 'measles'->'measles', 'zzzes'->'zzzes', 'gles'->'gles', 'qwertes'->'qwertes'. Note 'qwerte' -> 'qwertes' then 'qwertes' -> 'qwertes' (idempotent).
Line 3 is NOT always '3 X': for totals 1 and 2 it is '1 X' and '2 X'. Only totals >= 3 give '3 X'.
No format-string interpretation: --b '%s{}%d' -> '%s{}%ds'. A literal backslash-t in --b stays literal. A real embedded newline in --b splits the visible output into more than 5 physical lines.
result.confidence: High for everything about output formatting, the count->form relationship, and byte-level whitespace/newline behaviour: 238 counts were mechanically diffed against the model with zero mismatches, and all whitespace claims were checked with `cat -A` and `od -c`. High for the case-matcher branch order and the suffix rules (confirmed with synthetic nonsense stems, so they are not dictionary lookups). Two acknowledged gaps: (1) counts >= 131073 (hence any 7-digit count such as 1000001) are physically unreachable via execve, so 'no thousands separator' is proven only up to 6 digits and by locale-invariance, not at 1000001; (2) count 0 and negative counts are unreachable, so `count == 1` cannot be distinguished from `count <= 1`. Also indistinguishable by experiment: whether the case-matcher inspects the raw --b or the stripped --b (leading/trailing whitespace is caseless, so both give identical results on every input I could construct)."

rules: THERE ARE TWO DIFFERENT KINDS OF 'UNCHANGED'. (A) A verbatim early-return for already-plural words that returns the ORIGINAL argument string byte-for-byte (leading/trailing whitespace and arbitrary mixed case preserved). (B) The generic suffix rule endswith('es')->unchanged, which goes through strip()+lower()+re-case. Discriminator: pass '  WORD  ' (2 leading + 2 trailing spaces). If the output still has the spaces, WORD is in the already-plural set. Evidence: '  mice  '->'  mice  ' but '  boxes  '->'boxes'.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS (all steps confirmed): 1) cardinalize(unit,1) returns `unit` byte-for-byte, never touched (verified: line 4 == raw --b argument for all 1651 probes incl. whitespace/mixed case; 0 diffs). 2) pluralize computes norm = arg.strip().lower() (strip removes both spaces and TABs: '\tmice\t' and ' \t mice \t ' both round-trip verbatim). 3) EMPTY GUARD: if norm=='' return the ORIGINAL arg verbatim -- ''->'' , ' '->' ' , '   '->'   ' , '\t'->'\t'. It does NOT append 's'. 4) ALREADY-PLURAL EARLY RETURN: if norm is in the 99-member set below, return the ORIGINAL arg verbatim. 5) else if norm is a key of the irregular singular->plural map, result = mapped value. 6) else apply suffix rules to norm. 7) re-apply case pattern and return the STRIPPED result (whitespace is dropped on this path).
